issue_notes.body: ✅ issue-builder has started. You can view progress here.

Proposal for #22:

**Change**
- `src/helpers/utils.ts`: add `findPythonCommand()`. It probes `python3 --version`, then `python --version` (via `child_process.spawnSync`, no shell), and accepts the first one that reports `Python 3.x`. That also skips a `python` that is really Python 2. The result is cached per process.
- `getCompiledCommandToRun` uses it for `.py` files instead of the hard-coded `python`.
- If neither interpreter works, it throws `Python 3 was not found (tried python3, python). Install Python 3 to run <source>`. Solution, validator and generator callers already report a thrown error from this function as a failure to get the compiled command. So the user sees "Python is missing" and not a Runtime Error from `/bin/sh: python: not found`.

**Tests** (`tests/helpers/utils.test.ts`, with `child_process.spawnSync` mocked)
- Only `python` exists: the command starts with `python `.
- Both exist: `python3` is preferred.
- `python` is Python 2 and `python3` is absent: it is rejected.
- Neither exists: the call throws the "Python 3 was not found" error.

The "neither exists" test fails without the change, because today the command is built with `python` regardless. The "prefers python3" test fails too. I'll also update the existing `.py` tests so they don't depend on the host's interpreter.

**Not covered**
The `no-python-alias` corpus lane lives in `corpus/` and `.gitlab-ci.yml`, which I may not edit. I can't confirm that lane passes. I'll note that on the MR so a person can run it.

**Expected tier:** medium. `src/helpers/utils.ts` matches `src/**`, and the change is small. It isn't one of the high-tier paths such as `solution.ts` or `executor.ts`.

Go-ahead: someone other than @Ahmad-Faraj replies @ai-issue-builder-gitlab-ai-hackathon_e1c791 go-ahead on one line (@HamzaHassanain or @Mazen-Ghanaym)

@Mazen-Ghanaym the flows are re-synced with !25 (issue-builder 1.0.2). This is the Oct 20 check. Could you read the proposal above and, if it looks right, reply with its go-ahead line (the builder account and `go-ahead` on one line)? I filed #22, so it cannot be me. If something should change, say so here and the builder will post a revised proposal.
✅ issue-builder has started. You can view progress here.

Opened !26 (https://gitlab.com/gitlab-ai-hackathon/transcend-october-2026/30770856/showcase/-/merge_requests/26) from the go-ahead above. It follows the proposal: `findPythonCommand()` tries `python3`, then `python`, skips Python 2, and throws "Python 3 was not found" if neither exists. Lint, format check, vitest and build pass locally.

Next: the MR pipeline runs. Once it passes, a person mentions the reviewer on the MR (if it fails, the pipeline fixer). Each fix round needs its own go-ahead. I can't run the `no-python-alias` corpus lane, so someone should confirm it passes.

<details><summary>Details: findings, evidence, risk</summary>

**P1/P2:** none.

**Fixed in earlier rounds:** none (first review of this MR).

**Optional follow-ups (P3):**
- `src/helpers/utils.ts` `findPythonCommand`: only a successful lookup is cached. If Python 3 is missing, every `.py` object spawns `python3 --version` and `python --version` again (up to 5 s each on timeout). This is harmless for a CLI that fails on the first throw, but it could be cached too.
- `tests/helpers/utils.test.ts`: no test covers the version printed on stderr (the pre-3.4 branch), a non-zero exit status, or the spawn timeout. The `result.error || result.status !== 0` path is only exercised through ENOENT.
- `findPythonCommand` returns a bare command name and the shell resolves it again. This is fine, and the source path is still passed through `quoteShellArgument`, which the tests check.

**Review of the diff (done by me, no specialists at low risk):**
- `src/helpers/utils.ts` lines 507-552: `spawnSync` is called without a shell and with fixed arguments, so there is no injection surface. It skips a candidate on error or non-zero status and accepts it only when the output matches `/^Python 3\./m`. A Python 2 `python` is rejected. The thrown message matches the one in the tests.
- `getCompiledCommandToRun` (line 579) is the only changed call site. Callers I looked at (`checker.ts` 223, `solution.ts` 304/352/432/722, `validator.ts` 129/167/222/397) already call it inside try blocks. I did not check `generator.ts` 184.
- Tests: the `.py` cases are now independent of the host's interpreter (`child_process.spawnSync` is mocked). They cover python3 only, python-only fallback, python3 preferred, Python 2 rejected, a Python 2 `python3` skipped in favour of `python`, no interpreter, one lookup per process, and shell-quoting of the path. The cache is reset in `beforeEach` and `afterEach`.
